note: Arthur Little's front of 1889 for Wirt Dexter at 1721 Prairie Avenue, two years after it was built and thirteen before the 1904 scene. Read off the plate itself: a flat-fronted three-storey house over a low basement in a light, smooth wall, under a deep moulded cornice and a balustraded parapet with solid pedestals; its north part set back from the main front, with the entrance porch standing in that recess on two columns under a flat roof railed as a balcony, the door in the recessed wall; the main front stepping forward from it, the north return of that forward part carrying a tall plain chimney stack up past the parapet; on the forward front two segmental bows rising through the ground and second storeys, each roofed at the third floor as a balcony behind a balustrade; tall shuttered windows, iron balconettes at the ground-floor windows, small carved tablets over the upper windows; and on the north face of the recessed part an oval light and a window a storey. The 1911 Sanborn sheet draws the same plan (two curved bays on the front, a one-storey porch in a recess at the north-west corner), which is what this plate is read against.
what_it_supplies: the recess at the north end of the front, the entrance porch standing in it on two columns and its flat roof railed as a balcony
the forward block with two bows through two storeys, each topped by a balcony at the third floor
three storeys over a low basement, a flat roof behind a moulded cornice and a balustraded parapet
the tall stack on the forward block's north return
